Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Nevada, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Getting your ballot

Tuesday, October 20Passed

There is no request to make. To be sent a mail ballot, you had to register, or update your registration, no later than 14 days before the election: Tuesday, October 20, 2026. That date has passed. If you register after it (including at the polls), you vote in person instead of getting a ballot by mail. (the law)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

If you mail it: postmarked on or before Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026, and received by your county clerk by 5 p.m. on Saturday, November 7, 2026 (the fourth day after the election). If you hand it in: before the polls close on Election Day (7 p.m.). (the law)

That date has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Friday, October 30, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Nevada’s own page on voting by mail

At school away from home, in Nevada or in another state? What Nevada says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

You do not need to ask or give a reason. Your county clerk mails a ballot to every active registered voter for every election, unless the voter turned it down in writing at least 60 days before the election. (the law)

How to ask for a ballot

  • Automatically. If you are an active registered voter, a ballot is mailed to you without asking. For voters living in Nevada, ballots go out between Monday, October 5 and Monday, October 12, 2026. Anyone who registers or updates their registration no later than 14 days before the election is also mailed one. If yours has not come, contact your county clerk. (the law)
  • In person. You can also vote in person during early voting or on Election Day instead. If a mail ballot was sent to you, hand it in at the polling place or sign a statement that you have not already voted. (the law)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail it in the prepaid return envelope. It must be postmarked by Election Day and arrive by 5 p.m. on Saturday, November 7, 2026. If the postmark cannot be read, it counts if it arrives by 5 p.m. on Friday, November 6. (the law)
  • Drop box. Every polling place in Nevada, including early voting sites, has a ballot drop box. Counties may set up more. Drop it off before the polls close on Election Day. (the law)
  • In person. Hand it to your county clerk's office before the polls close on Election Day. You can also ask someone you trust to return it for you, by mail or in person; they must turn it in within three days, or by Election Day if they get it from you close to the election. (the law)

What the envelope needs

Sign the return envelope in the space for your signature. No witness or notary is needed. The county checks your signature against the ones on file; if it is missing or does not seem to match, the county will contact you, and you have until 5 p.m. on Monday, November 9, 2026 (the sixth day after the election) to fix it. If you registered by mail or online and have never voted in a federal election in Nevada, you may be told to put a copy of an ID or a document with your name and address in the return envelope. A person who has a disability, is 65 or older, or cannot read or write may have someone help mark and sign the ballot; that helper adds their name, address and signature to the envelope. (the law)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on Nevada’s own site (federal guide)

Vote early in person instead

Saturday, October 17, 2026 to Friday, October 30, 2026.

Early voting in person runs from Saturday, October 17, 2026 (the third Saturday before the election) through Friday, October 30, 2026. Sundays and federal holidays are left out unless your county adds them. Hours are set by each county. (the law)

Students

At school in Nevada, away from home

Nevada law says no one gains or loses their home for voting just because they are at, or away at, a school or college. You register at the street address where you actually live. Mail ballots are sent in envelopes that cannot be forwarded, so keep your address up to date with your county clerk. (the law)

At school in another state, with Nevada as home

The state's law does not speak to students in other states separately. Its general rule is that a person does not lose their Nevada home for voting by being away at a school or college, so a Nevada student at school in another state can stay registered in Nevada. Mail ballots are sent to the address the county has and are not forwarded, so such a student should contact their county clerk about where their ballot will be mailed. (the law)

Military and overseas

Military voters, their families and U.S. citizens living overseas can register and ask for a ballot with the Federal Post Card Application (by mail, email or fax) or through Nevada's online system at NVEASE.gov. FVAP's guide gives these 2026 dates: a ballot request through the online system by October 20, 2026 (passed) and by mail, email or fax received by October 21, 2026; registering through NVEASE.gov is open until the polls close on Election Day. A ballot returned by mail must be postmarked by Tuesday, November 3, 2026 and received by the fourth day after the election; one returned by email, fax or the online system must arrive by 7 p.m. on November 3. The Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot is a backup if your ballot does not come in time. (federal guide)

Nevada in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • Nevada mails a ballot to every active registered voter. If you have moved, or your ballot has not come, contact your county clerk; ballots are not forwarded to a new address.
  • The Nevada Secretary of State's own pages (nvsos.gov) did not answer our request, so this record is built from the Nevada Revised Statutes (current text, which shows amendments through 2025) and the federal FVAP guide. The ballot tracker's address is the one the FVAP guide gives. Check your county clerk for drop box and early voting locations and hours.
  • Polls in Nevada are open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. on Election Day (NRS 293.273).
